graded_figure.reason: The graded figure is the cross entropy the verifier's OWN nanoGPT parameters spend over its held-out FineWeb slice, divided by that slice's length in bytes. Producing it requires a 3250-step GPU training run over bytes that exist only inside the verifier image. solution/recompute.py invokes no model and reaches no such bytes, so it computes no graded figure and states none. The retired stand-in's 1.2532905300907615 was the add-lambda count-MLE reading over 6144 bytes of the synthetic word-cycle corpus; it is not comparable to the re-pinned measurement and is not carried forward.

local_replication.what_it_is: An ESTIMATE a solver can compute for itself, over the agent-visible corpus. It is not the graded figure and is never presented as one.

steps.detail: read frozen/model_config.json, frozen/optimizer_config.json, frozen/compute_budget.json, frozen/data_config.json and frozen/nanogpt_substrate.json, and note that one optimizer update is one nanoGPT step over 524288 tokens with exactly one forward and one backward pass, not one token consumed.
instruction.md states the graded quantity twice, as prose and as a formula, and both reduce to bits per byte over the verifier's held-out FineWeb slice from harness-owned model state.
only the tokenizer and its vocabulary may move. Widening the model, extending the corpus or spending more steps are all refused by name.

compute is fixed in steps and each step consumes 524288 tokens, so a coarser vocabulary buys more bytes of FineWeb per step. Merge frequent adjacent pairs until the marginal per-token cost outweighs the coverage gain.
byte-pair encoding over the agent-visible FineWeb training text at frozen/train_corpus.txt, deterministic tie-break, capped at max_token_bytes and max_vocab_size.

the graded split lives only in the verifier image, so no submission can measure the graded figure. Hold out your own slice of the agent-visible corpus, run the local replication recipe over it with the declared smoothing constant, and read an estimate off your own run.
write claim.json carrying the figure just computed. It earns nothing. Writing a lower figure instead would score zero with both numbers recorded.
write /app/submission.py so the verifier can run it alone, and let the verifier's own measurement be the graded number.
